job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many people believe that eating only one type of 'superfood' is enough to stay healthy, but this is a dangerous myth. A truly balanced diet requires a variety of food groups to provide all necessary nutrients. For instance, some think that roughage or fibre is useless because our bodies cannot digest it, but fibre is actually essential for smooth digestion and bowel health. Another common mistake is thinking that only oily snacks cause weight gain, while extra portions of rice or roti are harmless. In reality, the body converts any excess energy from carbohydrates into stored fat. Furthermore, many people mistakenly believe that white polished rice or maida are superior because they look cleaner and finer than whole grains. In truth, whole grains like millets and brown rice are far more nutritious as they retain the bran and germ. Finally, some assume that vegetarians cannot get enough protein without meat or eggs. This is incorrect, as pulses, legumes, and dairy are excellent plant-based protein sources that can easily meet our daily requirements. A balanced plate must include a mix of these diverse foods, tailored to your specific age and activity level, rather than following a one-size-fits-all approach.

items.evidence: In reality, the body converts any excess energy from carbohydrates into stored fat.
items.q: Meena never eats oily snacks, but she eats three extra rotis every day. What will most likely happen?
options: Her body will store the extra energy as fat
Her weight stays the same, since roti has no oil
Her body will pass out the extra roti as fibre
Her weight stays the same, since roti is a healthy grain
items.explain: The body turns any extra energy from carbohydrates like roti into stored fat, even without oily food.

wrong.why: thinks only oily food causes weight gain
mixes in the nearby idea that fibre is not digested
thinks a healthy food can be eaten in any amount

items.q: Our body cannot digest roughage. Why should we still eat foods rich in it?
options: It helps food move smoothly through the gut
It gives us more energy than vitamins do
It is not needed, so peeled foods are better
It turns into body fat when eaten extra
items.explain: Even though it is not digested, fibre is essential for smooth digestion and bowel health.

No, because white rice is cleaner and finer
No, because brown rice is a poor people's grain

items.explain: Whole grains like brown rice are more nutritious because they still have the bran and germ.
